title: Why Your Brain Turns Shapes Degree by Degree?
description:
Myth vs. Neural Mechanism — Roger Shepard & Jacqueline Metzler (1971): 3D Mental Rotation & the Linear 60-Degrees-Per-Second Mind's Eye, grounded in Roger N. Shepard, Jacqueline Metzler (1971) (Science). Empirical findings show that published in Science on February 19, 1971, Roger Shepard and Jacqueline Metzler tested eight adult participants across 1,600 trials each (200 trials per session across 8-10 sessions) viewing pairs of asymmetric 3D shapes built from ten connected solid cubes.

At the circuit level, this episode examines how parietal cortex, premotor cortex, primary visual cortex coordinate behavioral and neural responses, alongside evidence that on half the trials, the two 10-cube shapes were identical except rotated relative to each other by 0 to 180 degrees (in 20-degree steps); on the other half, one shape was an enantiomorph (3D mirror-image chiral twin) that could NEVER be rotated into congruence.

Primary Peer-Reviewed Sources:
- Roger N. Shepard, Jacqueline Metzler (1971). Mental Rotation of Three-Dimensional Objects. Science. https://doi.org/10.1126/science.171.3972.701
- Michael Peters, Christian Battista (2008). Applications of mental rotation figures of the Shepard and Metzler type and description of a mental rotation stimulus library. Brain and Cognition. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.bandc.2007.09.003
- Tomoaki Kozaki (2022). Training effect on sex-based differences in components of the Shepard and Metzler mental rotation task. Journal of Physiological Anthropology. https://doi.org/10.1186/s40101-022-00314-z

AI Disclosure: Visual reenactments, 3D anatomical models, and narration in this documentary Short were produced with AI synthesis tools from verified peer-reviewed sources.
